data.one_liner: A floating panel window that can be dragged, spring-snapped, parked off-edge, and tapped to grow.
data.what_it_does: Provides a draggable floating panel window for Flutter that spring-snaps to the nearest edge based on momentum, can stash off-screen into a grab tab, and expands in place when tapped. It uses physics-based spring motion and supports gesture control.
use_when: You need a floating picture-in-picture style player or mini-panel over your content.
You want panels that can snap to edges or stash off-screen into grab tabs.
avoid_when: Your app relies strictly on standard framework Material widgets without the standalone material_ui package.
You need a standard bottom sheet or modal dialog instead of a free-roaming floating window.
strengths: High-performance motion driven directly inside a RenderBox without widget rebuilds during animation.
Calculates drop targets and spring physics based on actual momentum and Apple-inspired fluid interfaces.
Persists resting position as intent rather than raw pixels across layout changes.
weaknesses: Requires the standalone material_ui package instead of standard package:flutter/material.dart.
expandedBuilder runs its layout up front, meaning expensive initialization inside the builder must be avoided.
data.setup_notes: Add draggable_panel and material_ui to pubspec.yaml. Mount the panel via MaterialApp.builder.
data.minimal_example:
MaterialApp(
  builder: (context, child) => DraggablePanel(
    collapsedBuilder: (context, status) => const Icon(Icons.play_arrow),
    expandedBuilder: (context, status) => const MiniPlayer(),
    child: child,
  ),
  home: const HomeScreen(),
)
